cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ, is wrapping up the letter he, Silvanus and Timothy sent to the church of the Thessalonians. He just told them the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, and he told them to encourage and build one another up. Now, at the very end, he's got a LIST, friend, and every job on it is BIG.

cards.question: Paul opens his final instructions with a request. Who does he ask the brothers to acknowledge?

answers.text: Those who work hard and care for them
Those who have believed the longest
Those who give the most to the church

cards.text: Paul says, "In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another." That last line takes three seconds to read and a LIFETIME to do, friend.

cards.question: Paul gives different people different care. He urges the brothers to admonish the unruly, ___ the fainthearted and help the weak.
Paul tells the brothers to be patient with each other but not with outsiders.
Now the hardest one on Paul's list. Somebody does you wrong, and your thumbs are ALREADY typing the reply in the group chat. What does Paul tell the brothers to make sure of?

answers.text: That no one repays evil for evil
That the leaders settle it quickly

cards.text: Instead, Paul says, "Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people." Then he goes rapid-fire, short commands, like a coach yelling from the sideline with two minutes on the clock.

cards.question: Paul's rapid-fire list opens with two short commands about joy and prayer. Which two?

answers.text: Always rejoice and never stop praying
Rejoice on good days and pray every morning
Rejoice in private and pray in public

cards.question: Paul says giving thanks in every circumstance is God's will for the brothers in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Paul says not to extinguish the Spirit and not to treat prophecies with contempt. Friend, you don't toss the WHOLE batch over one weird-looking cookie.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers not to treat prophecies with contempt. What does he say to do instead?
After testing everything, Paul says to hold fast to what is good but to avoid only the worst kinds of evil.

cards.text: Then Paul says, may the God of peace Himself sanctify them completely. Completely, friend, not a touch-up, and trust me, I know a little something about getting made new.

cards.question: Paul says may their entire spirit, soul and body be kept blameless at the ___ of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul says someone is faithful and will do it. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Brothers, pray for us as well." He also tells them to greet all the brothers with a holy kiss, and if I tried that, friend, all you'd get is a face full of MUSTACHE.

cards.question: Paul charges the brothers before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.

cards.text: And Paul signs off: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you." Short, sweet and sealed, baker, just like a cookie box ready to go.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but both wrong answers are invented categories rather than real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question never identifies whose spirit, soul and body Paul means. The pronoun "their" depends on earlier cards that are no longer on screen, so the question does not provide its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Will do it" has no antecedent within the question. Understanding what "it" means requires remembering the sanctification and preservation described on earlier cards.
